text:
Dear all

Thank you for your patience on this matter. Your marks for the mid-semester presentation are now available on Moodle.

We apologize for the delay even though it was mentioned earlier that the marks were ready .... changes were requested on the feedback given to mirror what is provided on MUA end and thus required a rewrite of the feedback to match as much as possible. This had to be done across BOTH FYP parts 1 and 2 thus incurring the delay.

General feedback on the impact of rubric changes towards your presentation assessments

1. As you will see in your gradebook, breakdown of marks is not provided and will not be released. Only category grade scores are available for your reference and the final grade mark achieved.
2. Getting a category grade score of "Below passing grade / Did not show enough evidence to be graded competent" does not mean that you scored zero. It means the marks for that particular category was below a mappable category (i.e. below 50/100).
3. We have explained all the additional rubrics in last and this week's studios - if you did not attend any of the sessions, you may ask around to students who did to figure out how to fix the issues listed in feedback.
4. Majority of penalties applied to students presenting include (a) holding a handphone during presentation and/or (b) reading from notes/script. Not being dressed appropriately also incurs a penalty which falls into professional conduct. Whilst we are not expecting formal dressing, attending a graded assessment in slippers and shorts shows poor professionalism on your part.
5. Other penalties will be for teams exceeding time. We limited this by stopping the presentation entirely after one (1) minute to avoid deducting too many marks (every minute is a 5% deduction to final score)
6. The teams did fairly well and were consistent with the rubrics but the stricter categorization of items meant a lower overall score. Completing the items as required will only give teams/students a passing (P/C) grade. Going above and beyond to really show something outside of regular effort is what now gains the higher grades of D and HD.

All this is in line with the university requesting for proof to really show that a D or HD capstone project really deserves that grade assigned and it does not look like just a completed assignment from a regular unit.

Although there is a large overlap between both, we tend to favour the following distinction between them where requirements = what you need to do to satisfy goals and goals = what you need to deliver (i.e. deliverables). Requirements : login/logout functions, create account functions, reporting functions, application for grant functions, etc

author: Soo Wooi King
text:
Studios for week 4 have completed and topics have been assigned to all teams.

By the end of the week, you should have (hopefully) reached out to your topic supervisors and started the process of getting details of the topic assigned. Majority of supervisors will NOT be emailing you or doing anything on their part .....since its not their grade anyway. Topic swaps are also no longer allowed as setup has been completed onto Moodle.

You will need to prepare a draft pitch deck / presentation slides by the end of week 5 that shows you have understood the (1) project requirements, (2) project goals / objectives / outcomes / deliverables, (3) project limitations / scopes / constraints, (4) any other vital information as listed in further detail below.

This pitch deck slides are uploaded onto Moodle for the signoff which is handled by your own team supervisors. The content will focus on your team being able to present 3 aspects of the project: the scope, how you use WSM and project goals

Ignoring the flow as in the written worksheet (which may not suit some topics in MUM) the suggested content in your slides is as follows ...adjust accordingly

1. Introduction slide
2. Problem statement / Opportunity statement - what your project is trying to solve or what your project sees as a opportunity for development/exploration
3. Project overview - general summary of what your project is trying to do in reference to (2)
4. Analysis of Option and Recommendation - implement WSM and show at least one example to decide on project directions
5. Preliminary project requirements / objectives - what you have extracted from your supervisors, decided upon, planned to use etc.
6. Project goals (SMART) / deliverables - as above in 3 but what will be the output at the very end of the project (i.e. after part 2)
7. Project limitations / scope - typically scope = something you set to be achieved due to certain reasons (i.e. what is in-scope/achievable or out-of-scope / not achievable), limitations = restrictions or constraints on the project that is often out of your control. This varies between projects and may overlap.
8. Schedule estimate / timeline
9. Conclusions - what is still pending that needs further investigation, elaboration etc.

Complete the deck and upload on Moodle under the sign-offs. Ping your supervisor to sign-off on the content. If there is no sign off the subsequent presentation sessions are considered invalid and no marks will be awarded even though the presentation was executed. Teams are free to continue updating and correcting their slides until the actual presentation.

NOTE: Presentation scheduling will be in a separate post coming soon
